checkpoints.description: Task 'review-fixes-2-v1' completed successfully.

[1/1] Import Dict in scripts/aikit_cli.py, whose project_is_clean and project_payload annotations name it without importing it; add a unit-tier guard that forces every annotation in scripts/ to evaluate, so a name that only resolves under Python 3.14's deferred annotations fails here; ADR-181 records the incident and the CI outage.

impact_assessment.why: Commit e18a1b3 (ADR-172) annotated two functions with Dict but never imported it. Python 3.14 evaluates annotations lazily (PEP 649), so nothing on the only local interpreter noticed; Python 3.10 to 3.13, which the README states as supported and CI tests, evaluate them when def runs, so importing scripts.aikit_cli raises NameError and every aikit.py command fails. It has been on origin since push 9653975, and GitHub Actions caught nothing because the account is locked for billing and no CI step has run since at least 10-19.
impact_assessment.benefits: aikit.py works again on every supported Python; a guard that runs on 3.14 catches the whole class of deferred-annotation NameError, which matters most while CI cannot run.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none, a missing import is restored. dependency: none. concurrency: none. state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Prove the bug with a failing-first guard that reproduces Python 3.10-3.13's eager evaluation on 3.14 by reading every function and class __annotations__; confirm the simulation flags exactly the two known annotations and nothing else; keep the guard spawn-free and inside the unit tier's 10ms per-test budget.

Task 'py310-annotations-v1' completed successfully.

[1/4] check_secrets: list tracked files with ls-files -z and run git with core.quotePath=false, so --all scans non-ASCII names and diff findings name their file; integration test with a real repo. [2/4] Refuse a line break in a project gate command or a UI contract command at load, since Windows cmd runs only the first line. [3/4] README gate: in a repository that has aikit.py, a missing scripts/aikit_parser.py is an error instead of a silent skip. [4/4] aikit check pushes only with --push; --no-push stays accepted; README, runbook, services.md and ADR-182 updated.

impact_assessment.why: The last-five-push review found: check_secrets --all silently skips every tracked file with a non-ASCII name because git quotes it, and its diff modes lose the file name; a multi-line command reports success on Windows after running only its first line; the README command check would switch itself off silently if the grammar file were renamed; and aikit check pushes by default although the runbook makes it a project's Phase 4 and PRINCIPLE-018 R4 pushes only when authorized. The user asked to fix the rest; CI cannot run, so local gates are the only verification.
impact_assessment.benefits: The secret sweep covers every tracked file and names every finding; a gate command behaves the same on Windows and POSIX or is refused; a verification check cannot disable itself unnoticed; running Phase 4 can no longer publish to a remote as a side effect.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: aikit check stops pushing unless --push is given, a deliberate behaviour change to a documented command; commands containing a line break, previously accepted, are now refused with exit 2; check_secrets output labels change for non-ASCII paths. dependency: none. concurrency: none. state: no persisted data.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for each milestone, the secret one against a real git repository; keep --no-push accepted so existing scripts do not break; name the changed auto-push test in ADR-182 under PRINCIPLE-014 R3; refuse line breaks with a Why/Fix that says how to join steps; commit each milestone separately and verify each alone.

[1/1] verify_commit: choose the Fix line by where the failing commit is - already on the remote: fix forward; not HEAD: fix forward; unpushed HEAD: the existing git reset --soft HEAD^ advice; ADR-186.

impact_assessment.why: Reviewing the five pushes before the last five: verify_commit, introduced in 9a95501, printed 'git reset --soft HEAD^' for every failing commit. Verifying 83b67de, which is on origin, with HEAD at 7003657 told the user to undo a different, passing commit.
impact_assessment.benefits: The advice a failing verification prints is safe to follow wherever the commit is.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the Fix line text changes for a failing commit that is pushed or is not HEAD; exit codes and gates unchanged. dependency: none. concurrency: none. state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for both new branches with an extended fake runner that models the upstream check; the existing unpushed-HEAD test keeps its reset assertion; checked on the real published commit.

[1/4] check --push exits 1 when the requested push is skipped or refused; the three dirty-tree tests expect 1; a refused-push test; a test that fix never pushes; ADR-187. [2/4] verify_commit treats a commit any remote-tracking branch contains as pushed; the annotation guard also reads module-level annotations; a guard for f-string syntax Python 3.10 rejects; ADR-188 corrects ADR-181, ADR-182, ADR-186 and three commit messages. [3/4] run_shell refuses NUL; the ledger audit unquotes git's quoted paths; hygiene, update_knowledge_base and verify_commit print UTF-8 on Windows; ADR-189. [4/4] Full re-verification of every commit, then report.

impact_assessment.why: The verification of the nine unpushed commits found nine issues, each reproduced, with every proposed fix tested; the stop hook and the user's standing pattern call for fixing what is found. Re-checking the private-attribute rule showed its 12 production hits in neurocore are the singleton idiom, so widening it would flag correct code and the recommendation is withdrawn.
impact_assessment.benefits: An explicit --push that fails is reported as a failure; the reset advice cannot target a published commit; the 3.10 guards cover module annotations and PEP 701 f-strings; no command crashes on a NUL; ledger reports name real paths, spaces included; project gate output keeps non-ASCII names.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: check --push now exits 1 when its push does not happen; status --json reports unquoted paths; Fix text changes for a pushed commit without upstream. dependency: none. concurrency: none. state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: A failing-first test per fix; the changed test expectations named in ADR-187 under PRINCIPLE-014 R3; the path unquoting is a pure function tested on git's own quoted output; every commit verified alone.
